node.title: Re^2: Sometimes undef is initialized and sometimes not when hash values are fed to grep
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
This data is checked carefully on input and output. When undef gets somehow into hash then error is thrown.

Ok, I see. Although of course there are exceptions, I find it easiest to work with hashes in one of two ways: either a fixed set of possible keys, in which case one can avoid autovivification issues by not differentiating between [doc://exists] and [doc://defined], so it doesn't matter whether a key is present or not, and undef simply indicates "no value". Or, the other situation is a set of keys that is unknown to the code beforehand, in which case one generally only iterates over the hash with [doc://keys] etc., and one doesn't generally access specific hash keys by name.

It sounds like you might be mixing these two - although there are sometimes valid cases where a hash has a known set of keys and one does want to differentiate between [doc://exists] and [doc://defined], I've found this to be a little annoying to work with. For example, in my module [mod://IPC::Run3::Shell], there are options that can be exists but not defined, but then there is no easy way to override these options so they no longer exist in the hash.

Anyway, In the code you showed, I might have gone with [doc://exists] checks to prevent autoviv, even if that makes the code more verbose.
